props.gloss_en: the mishna (15b): all slaughter, and one may always slaughter
'all slaughter' means: all are [subject] to slaughter, even a bird
Rabba: the tanna of 'one may always slaughter' is R' Yishmael
R' Yishmael: 'when the Lord your God expands your border... and you say I will eat meat' (Deut 12:20) comes only to permit them meat of desire
R' Yishmael: at first, meat of desire was forbidden to them
R' Yishmael: once they entered the Land, meat of desire was permitted to them
Rabba: now that they are exiled, one might think they revert to the first prohibition -- therefore the mishna says 'one may always slaughter' [meat of desire]
Rav Yosef: [on that reading] this clause should have said 'one may always slaughter AND EAT'
Rav Yosef: why was it forbidden at first? because they were near the Tabernacle
Rav Yosef: why was it permitted in the end? because they were far from the Tabernacle
Rav Yosef: all the more so now [in exile], when they are farther still -- meat of desire is permitted
Rav Yosef: rather, the tanna of 'one may always slaughter' is R' Akiva
R' Akiva: 'if the place is too far from you... you shall slaughter of your herd and flock' (Deut 12:21) comes only to forbid them meat of stabbing
R' Akiva: at first, meat of stabbing was permitted to them
R' Akiva: once they entered the Land, meat of stabbing was forbidden to them
Rav Yosef: now that they are exiled, one might think they revert to the first permission -- therefore the mishna says 'one must always slaughter'
R' Akiva holds: meat of desire was never forbidden at all
R' Yishmael holds: meat of stabbing was never permitted at all
'and he shall slaughter the young bull' (Lev 1:5)
'shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them' (Num 11:22)
the mishna (85a): one who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand, and one who stabs or rips, is exempt from covering [the blood]
'only as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so shall you eat it' (Deut 12:22)
R' Yirmeya: limbs of stabbed meat that Israel brought with them into the Land -- what is their law?
in the seven years of conquest, even non-kosher food was permitted to them
'and houses full of all good things' (Deut 6:11)
Rav (via R' Yirmeya bar Abba): ['all good things' are] cuts of pig meat
rather, R' Yirmeya's question concerns the period after [the seven years]
alternatively: [the question is] in the seven years after all -- what was permitted them was the spoil of gentiles; their own was not permitted
the mishna (15b): one may slaughter with anything
Rabba: 'with anything' is taught like the other two clauses -- if they concern those who slaughter, so does it; if those slaughtered, so does it
Rava: 'all slaughter' -- one [such clause] includes a Kuti, and one includes an apostate Jew
Rava: 'one may always slaughter' -- by day and by night, on a rooftop and atop a ship
Rava: 'with anything' -- with flint, with glass, with the stalk of a reed

objections.gloss_en: שנית הכל שוחטין ולעולם שוחטין, בכל שוחטים מאי משנית ליה? וכי תימא בין בצור... הא דומיא דהנך קתני -- the clauses must be read alike, and 'with anything' cannot be read of the slaughtered
